newsitem.title: FRANCE: French Communist party chief, predecessor probed.
newsitem.headline: French Communist party chief, predecessor probed.

text.p: Robert Hue, head of the French Communist Party, and his predecessor Georges Marchais have been formally placed under investigation for alleged influence peddling, justice sources said on Monday.
France has been rocked by a string of political funding scandals in recent years, affecting all mainstream parties. But none has reached so high into a party's leadership.
The sources said the probe led by Paris magistrate Laurence Vichnievsky was part of an investigation into illicit funding of the Communist Party.
The sources said the two politicians were placed under investigation last week. The step could lead to a trial but does not imply guilt.

The magistrate had searched Communist Party headquarters in June in a probe over the disappearance of nearly 13 million francs ($2.5 million) in suspicious billing paid by the French utilities giant Compagnie Generale des Eaux (CGE) in 1992-1994 when some 70 mainly leftist towns were preparing to award water contracts.
In May, four former managers of the private consulting firm Sicopar, a subsidiary of the Gifco group, were placed under investigation in connection with the case on suspicion of acting as middlemen.
A Communist Party official at the time denied any wrongdoing. "Its finances are healthy and totally transparent," party treasurer Pierre Sotura said.
CGE's deputy general manager, Jean-Dominique Deschamps, has also been placed under investigation in the case.
